step.title: How much did you sell last month?
step.body: Most owners answer this by adding up a drawer of receipts. Let us do it in three clicks instead - and then read what the number is actually made of.

step.title: Open Reporting
step.body: In the main menu. Every report in the product lives behind this one item.

step.title: The period, set once
step.body: We have set it to Last Month for you. Every tab on this page obeys it, so you pick the period once and read all thirteen reports against it.

step.title: That is the month
step.body: Every order from every till, delivery app and counter, added up. Nothing was typed in to produce it.

step.title: Sold is not the same as collected
step.body: This is the money that actually arrived. The difference between the two tiles is what is still owed to you - the figure most restaurants never see.

step.title: And which days did the work
step.body: The same month, day by day. This is the chart that tells you which nights to staff properly and which to close early.

step.title: You just read a month of trading
step.body: Sold, collected, owed, and the shape of the month. Next: whether any of it was profit.

step.title: Revenue is not profit
step.body: A busy month can lose money, and it usually takes an accountant three weeks to say so. Here it is one tab away.

step.title: Click Profit
step.body: In the row of tabs above. It keeps the period you already chose, so this is still last month.

step.title: Everything that came in
step.body: Paid orders, plus anything you logged as income by hand - a catering job, a room hire. Both count, so the total is the real one.

step.title: Everything that went out
step.body: Your purchase orders and your logged running costs together. Mission 5 and 6 are where these two numbers come from.

step.title: What you actually kept
step.body: One figure, and the only one that decides whether the month was worth opening the doors for.

step.title: And where it went
step.body: Line by line, so a bad month names its own cause instead of leaving you guessing.

step.title: You now know if last month paid
step.body: In and out and what is left. Next: whether your storeroom agrees with your books.

step.title: What is in the storeroom right now?
step.body: Running out mid-service costs you the table and the reputation. This screen tells you the day before it happens.

step.title: Click Inventory Health
step.body: Same row of tabs. This one ignores the date filter on purpose - stock is what you have now, not what you had.

step.title: The only number that needs you today
step.body: Items at or under the reorder level you set. If this is not zero, somebody should be on the phone to a supplier.

step.title: Money sitting on the shelves
step.body: Stock is cash you have already spent. Knowing the figure is how you stop over-ordering the things that keep and under-ordering the things that sell.

step.title: Low stock first, always
step.body: The list sorts itself so the trouble is at the top. You can print it as an A4 sheet or a till roll and hand it to whoever does the buying.

step.title: The storeroom, without walking to it
step.body: That is the reading done. Now the working - and it starts at the till.

mission.title: Take a sale, end to end

step.title: Ring up an order and get paid for it
step.body: The whole loop: take the order at the till, watch it appear on the orders board, mark it served, and collect the money. Everything you have just been reading is made of this.

step.title: Open the POS
step.body: This is the screen your counter staff live on all day.

step.title: Tap any dish
step.body: One tap adds it. Tap the same dish again for a second portion - no quantity box, because a counter at seven in the evening has no time for one.

step.title: The bill builds itself
step.body: Quantities, a note for the kitchen, a discount on one line or on the lot - and the tax and the total recalculated as you go.

step.title: Place the order
step.body: It goes to the kitchen screen and the orders board in the same instant. This is a real order in the demo restaurant - go ahead.

step.title: And here it is, on the board
step.body: The till brought you straight here. Dine-in, takeaway and delivery all arrive in this one list, in the order they came in - and Orders, in the main menu, is how you get back to it.

step.title: Two badges, two questions
step.body: Every order carries where the food is up to and whether the money has arrived. They move separately, because in a real restaurant they do.

step.title: Move the food along
step.body: Press the green button on the ringed order to push it to its next stage - cooking, ready, served. The kitchen screen follows along.

step.title: Collect the payment
step.body: Press Pay on that same order.

step.title: How the money arrived
step.body: Cash, card or bKash, with room for a transaction id. Or send it out on account - the order stays open as a due, and it is the due that shows up as the gap in your sales report. Take the payment or close the box; either way the tour carries on.

step.title: One sale, all the way through
step.body: Taken, cooked, served, paid - and it has already changed the sales and profit figures you read at the start.

step.title: Buying is half of the profit line
step.body: A purchase order does three jobs at once: it tells the supplier what you want, it puts the stock on the shelf when it lands, and it puts the cost in the accounts. Let us raise one.

step.title: Open Inventory
step.body: Items, suppliers, recipes, waste and purchase orders all sit behind this one.

step.title: Go to Purchase Orders
step.body: The card for purchase orders, on this page.

step.title: Start a new order
step.body: Create PO, at the top right.

step.title: Who you are buying from
step.body: Suppliers are searchable by name or contact. Every order you place against one builds a history you can hold them to.

step.title: What you are buying
step.body: Pick an item, a quantity and a unit price, and add as many lines as you need. The order total adds itself up as you type - and when the delivery is received, every one of these lines goes onto the shelf.

step.title: That is your buying under control
step.body: Ordered, received, stocked and costed, without anybody writing it twice. Next: the costs that do not arrive on a lorry.

step.title: Rent, gas, wages - and the odd job
step.body: Not every taka moves through the till. Log the rest here and the profit figure you read in mission two becomes the truth rather than an estimate.

step.title: Open Accounting
step.body: Ledgers, income, expenses, tax rules and headers.

step.title: Go to Expenses
step.body: The expenses card on this page.

step.title: Log an expense
step.body: Log Expense, at the top right. Try it with anything - a gas bill, a repair.

step.title: A header, a category, an amount
step.body: The header is what your accountant will group it under; the category is what you call it. Save it and it lands in the profit report immediately.

step.title: Income works identically
step.body: This is the Income screen, and it is the same form. Anything you earn away from the till - a catering job, a hall booking - belongs here so it counts toward the month.

step.title: Your books now agree with your restaurant
step.body: Sales from the till, purchases from suppliers, and everything else by hand. One last thing, and it is the one worth remembering.

step.title: You can always start this again
step.body: Close it whenever you like and go and press things yourself - the tour keeps your place. Here is where it lives so you can find it again.

step.title: Open My Profile
step.body: Right at the bottom of the main menu.

step.title: This card, on your profile
step.body: It remembers where you got to - against you, not against this browser. Close the tour on your phone and pick it up on a laptop at the same step.

step.title: Continue, or start over
step.body: Continue picks up at the step you left. Start over goes back to the first mission - useful when you want to show somebody else.

step.title: That is the whole product
step.body: Reports, till, orders, buying and books - and you worked every one of them yourself. The tour is on your profile whenever you want it back, and there is one last thing worth saying before you go.

step.title: Now do it with your own menu
step.body: Everything you just used belongs to a made-up restaurant. Start your own free trial and it is the same screens with your food, your stock and your prices - add a few dishes and take one real sale, and the reports from the first mission start filling with your numbers. It is free for seven days, there is no card to enter, and it opens the moment you say yes.
